claim: Garleanu and Pedersen (NBER w15205, 2009; Journal of Finance 2013): with predictable returns and transaction costs the optimal policy trades partially towards an aim portfolio at a fixed rate a/lambda < 1 that falls with costs and rises with risk aversion (Proposition 2, eq. 7-10); the aim is an exponential average of current and expected future Markowitz portfolios, so predictors with slower alpha decay get more weight (Proposition 3). In their commodity-futures application (Table II, benchmark costs) the Markowitz portfolio has gross Sharpe 0.83 and net -9.84, the dynamic optimum 0.62 gross / 0.58 net, and the best static partial-adjustment rule (3% weight on Markowitz per day) 0.58 / 0.46; the dynamic net Sharpe is about 20% above the best static strategy because it under-weights the fast (2.4-day half-life) signal.
impact_on_spec: Rules P2, P3 and P2V are the static fixed-rate form of Proposition 2 applied per tranche to the unchanged M0 target; the persistence-tilted aim (Proposition 3) is deferred to a later contract because it changes the composite.
independent_replication: JKMP (SFI 22-63) extends the same aim-portfolio solution to stock portfolios with ML forecasts (eq. 20-21) and reports a net Sharpe about 20% above a two-stage static alternative; no independent replication on a weekly rank-weighted U3000 book was found.
limitations: Commodity futures, daily data, quadratic costs and a 5-day signal; our book is weekly, mostly slow signals, with spread plus square-root impact, so the size of the gain does not transfer, only the form of the rule.
quote: predictors with slower mean reversion (alpha decay) get more weight in the aim portfolio

claim: Novy-Marx and Velikov (A Taxonomy of Anomalies and Their Trading Costs, August 2015 version; RFS 2016), 1973-2012 with effective-spread costs: a buy/hold spread (a stricter rule to enter a position than to keep it, e.g. 10%/20% deciles) is the most effective cost-mitigation technique; for a UMD-like factor it earns 0.77%/month gross, 0.26% costs, 0.51% net, against 0.62 / 0.26 / 0.37 for staggered quarterly partial rebalancing and 0.66 / 0.35 / 0.31 for trading only a low-cost universe (Table 5): the same cost saving as lower-frequency staggered rebalancing while giving up less gross return.
impact_on_spec: Rules N25 and N50 are the continuous-weight analogue (a no-trade band around each name's target); v1.2's five weekly tranches are already a form of staggered partial rebalancing, which this paper ranks below the buy/hold spread.
independent_replication: Detzel, Novy-Marx and Velikov (JF 2023) and Chen-Velikov (JFQA 2023) use the same cost-mitigated construction; not re-read in this round.
limitations: Decile sorts with monthly rebalancing and 1973-2012 effective spreads; a band on continuous rank weights is an analogue, not the tested rule; 10%/20% in rank terms is roughly a 0.44 standard-deviation band in normal scores at the 80th-90th percentile, which motivates the 0.25 and 0.50 band sizes.
quote: introducing a buy/hold spread generally yields transaction cost reductions similar to those achieved with trading at lower frequency

claim: Jensen, Kelly, Malamud and Pedersen (SFI 22-63, 2022 version; RFS 2026): portfolios that put ML return forecasts, risk and trading costs into one objective keep positive out-of-sample net Sharpe ratios, reaching 1.38 for Portfolio-ML for an investor whose wealth reaches $10 billion by 2020, while cost-agnostic Markowitz portfolios fall to negative net returns.
impact_on_spec: Sets the realistic ceiling for a cost-aware book and supports one optimizer holding alpha, risk and costs (design section 8); M3 (random-feature ridge) follows this line. For v1.3 (2026-10-04): eq. (20) 'start from the grown position inherited from last period, and then trade toward an aim portfolio' is the form of rules P2/P3/P2V (drifted tranche weights as the starting point).
independent_replication: Authors' code is public (github theisij/ml-and-the-implementable-efficient-frontier); AQR Alternative Thinking 2024 Q4 reports gains from ML-built stock portfolios; no independent academic replication was read.
limitations: 2022 working-paper version (the RFS 2026 numbers may differ); price-impact costs only; a $10 billion large-cap investor, not a $1M U3000 book; the full model set needs about 75 GB, so we run a reduced version.

impact_on_spec: Single anomalies are not worth trading alone after costs; only cost-aware combinations can clear the bar, which is why the book replaces standalone anomaly tests.
independent_replication: Consistent with Jensen-Kelly-Pedersen (JF 2023) on replication versus profitability; not re-run here.
limitations: Spread costs only (no impact, no short-sale fees); anomaly portfolios as published; the date is the issue month.

impact_on_spec: Supports the impact term Y * sigma_daily * sqrt(Q/V) with Y = 0.5 in cost model v1 (design section 7) and the small impact at a $1M book.

limitations: Proprietary execution data, not replicable; algorithmic institutional execution, not market-on-open orders at the first print; month-level date.
